A Visual Guide to Mushroom Safety & Traits - A Case Study

Cheng Peng

West Chester University


1 Introduction

This assignment focuses on building interactive dashboards and story points using Tableau Public. The goal is to help users explore a hypothetical data set of 61,069 mushrooms—representing 173 species, with 353 specimens per species—to understand how physical and ecological traits relate to edibility versus poison risk. Of the 20 variables, 17 are nominal and 3 are metrical.

Variable Name Description
cap-diameter (m) float number in cm
cap-shape (n) bell=b, conical=c, convex=x, flat=f, sunken=s, spherical=p, others=o
cap-surface (n) fibrous=i, grooves=g, scaly=y, smooth=s, shiny=h, leathery=l, silky=k, sticky=t, wrinkled=w, fleshy=e
cap-color (n) brown=n, buff=b, gray=g, green=r, pink=p, purple=u, red=e, white=w, yellow=y, blue=l, orange=o, black=k
does-bruise-bleed (n) bruises-or-bleeding=t, no=f
gill-attachment (n) adnate=a, adnexed=x, decurrent=d, free=e, sinuate=s, pores=p, none=f, unknown=?
gill-spacing (n) close=c, distant=d, none=f
gill-color (n) see cap-color + none=f
stem-height (m) float number in cm
stem-width (m) float number in mm
stem-root (n) bulbous=b, swollen=s, club=c, cup=u, equal=e,rhizomorphs=z, rooted=r
stem-surface (n) see cap-surface + none=f
stem-color (n) see cap-color + none=f
veil-type (n) partial=p, universal=u
veil-color (n) see cap-color + none=f
has-ring (n) ring=t, none=f
ring-type (n) cobwebby=c, evanescent=e, flaring=r, grooved=g, large=l, pendant=p, sheathing=s, zone=z, scaly=y, movable=m, none=f, unknown=?
spore-print-color (n) see cap color
habitat (n) grasses=g, leaves=l, meadows=m, paths=p, heaths=h, urban=u, waste=w, woods=d
season (n) spring=s, summer=u, autumn=a, winter=w
class poisonous=p, edible=e (binary target variable)

\(^*\) n: nominal, m: metrical; nominal values as sets of values

2 Data Story and Prototyping

2.1 Data Story Formulation

Goal: Help users explore 61,069 hypothetical mushrooms (173 species, 353 each) to understand how physical and ecological traits relate to edibility vs. poison risk.

Data Story is based on the following 4 questions:

  • Q1: How common are edible vs. poisonous mushrooms?
  • Q2: Do certain cap colors signal danger more often?
  • Q3: Can stem dimensions help predict edibility?
  • Q4: When and where are you most likely to find edible mushrooms?

2.2 Dashboard Prototyping

Individual Carts Corresponding to Questions

  • Chart Q1 - Edibility Overview – Donut Chart for distributional information:
    • Visual: Donut chart showing % edible (e) vs. poisonous (p + unknown).
    • Interactivity: Click on a segment to filter all other charts.
    • Why start here: Sets the baseline risk context.
  • Chart Q2 -Cap Color × Edibility – Stacked Bar Chart- Relationship between two categorical variables:
    • Visual: Cap color (n=12 colors) on x-axis, stacked bars for e/p.
    • Interactivity: Hover shows counts; clicking a color filters charts 3 & 4.
    • Insight example: Red/e might be safer than red/p.
  • Chart Q3 - Stem Height & Width – Scatter Plot (colored by edibility)
    • Axes: X = stem-height (cm), Y = stem-width (mm).
    • Color: e = green, p = red.
    • Interactivity: Brush/zoom to select a region → filters chart 4.
    • Note: 3 metrical variables (cap-diameter, stem-height, stem-width) live here.
  • Chart Q4 - Season × Habitat – Heatmap (edibility rate)
    • Rows: Season (spring/summer/autumn/winter)
    • Columns: Habitat (grasses, leaves, woods, urban, etc.)
    • Cell value: % edible in that season+habitat combination.
    • Interactivity: Click a cell to highlight matching mushrooms in chart 3.

Interconnection Flow - How charts talk to each other

Action Effect
Click “edible” in chart 1 Charts 2–4 show only edible mushrooms
Select a cap color in chart 2 Charts 3–4 filtered to that color
Brush points in chart 3 Chart 4 highlights relevant season/habitat
Click a heatmap cell in chart 4 Chart 3 zooms to those stem dimensions

Dashboard Layout

+------------------------------------------------+
|  Title: Mushroom Safety Explorer               |
+------------------------------------------------+
|  [Chart Q1]        |  [Chart Q2]               |
|  Edibility Donut   |  Cap Color Stacked Bar    |
|                    |                           |
+--------------------+---------------------------+
|  [Chart Q3]                                    |
|  Stem Height vs. Width Scatter                 |
|  (brush to select)                             |

3 Tableau Implementation - Step-by-step Procedure

📥 Data Preparation

  • Download/Prepare data (mushroom dataset with 61,069 rows)

  • Open Tableau Public → Connect → Text/Excel → Select your file

  • Create a new worksheet → name it 1_Edibility_Donut

  • Create calculated field with name Edibility Status (for edibility grouping):

    IF [class] = 'e' THEN 'Edible'
    ELSE 'Poisonous'
    END
  • Create calculated field with name Number of Records(Counting the number of observations for percentage of total):
    COUNT([reduced-mushroom.csv])
  • Re-code Cap.Color: Create calculated field with name CapColor
IF [Cap.Color] = "n" THEN "brown"
ELSEIF [Cap.Color] = "b" THEN "buff"
ELSEIF [Cap.Color] = "g" THEN "gray"
ELSEIF [Cap.Color] = "r" THEN "green"
ELSEIF [Cap.Color] = "p" THEN "pink"
ELSEIF [Cap.Color] = "u" THEN "purple"
ELSEIF [Cap.Color] = "e" THEN "red"
ELSEIF [Cap.Color] = "w" THEN "white"
ELSEIF [Cap.Color] = "y" THEN "yellow"
ELSEIF [Cap.Color] = "l" THEN "blue"
ELSEIF [Cap.Color] = "o" THEN "orange"
ELSEIF [Cap.Color] = "k" THEN "black"
ELSE [Cap.Color]
END
  • Re-code Habitat: Create calculated field with name Habitat0
IF [Habitat] = "g" THEN "Grasses"
ELSEIF [Habitat] = "l" THEN "Leaves"
ELSEIF [Habitat] = "m" THEN "Meadows"
ELSEIF [Habitat] = "p" THEN "Paths"
ELSEIF [Habitat] = "h" THEN "Heaths"
ELSEIF [Habitat] = "u" THEN "Urban"
ELSEIF [Habitat] = "w" THEN "Waste"
ELSEIF [Habitat] = "d" THEN "Woods"
ELSE "Unknown"
  • Re-code Season: Create calculated field with name Season0
IF [season] = "s" THEN "Spring"
ELSEIF [season] = "u" THEN "Summer"
ELSEIF [season] = "a" THEN "Autumn"
ELSEIF [season] = "w" THEN "Winter"
ELSE "Unknown"
END

📊 Chart Q2 – Cap Color vs. Edibility (Stacked Bar Chart)

Step Action
1 Create a new worksheet → name it 2-Edibility-CapColor
2 Drag cap-color to Columns
3 Drag Number of Records to Rows
4 Drag Edibility Status to Color on the Marks card
5 Change Mark type to Bar (if not already automatic)
6 Sort bars (largest to smallest):
• Right-click cap-color on Columns → Sort
• Sort by: Field → Number of Records → Descending
7 Add labels:
• Drag Number of Records to Label
• Right-click the label → Quick Table Calculation → Percent of Total
8 Format colors:
• Edible = Green
• Poisonous = Red

• Cap color: <cap-color>
• Edibility: <Edibility Status>
• Count: <CNT(Number of Records)>

• Right-click the Y-axis → Edit Axis → Title = Number of Mushrooms


📉 Chart 3 – Stem Height vs. Stem Width (Scatter Plot)

Step Action
1 New worksheet → name 3_Stem_Scatter
2 Drag stem-height to Columns
3 Drag stem-width to Rows
4 Drag Edibility Status to Color
5 Change Mark type to Circle
6 Adjust opacity (very important for overlapping points):
• Click Color → Effects → Opacity = 50%
7 Drag cap-diameter to Size (optional – adds 3rd metric)
8 Add trend lines:
• Analytics pane → Drag Trend Line to view → choose Linear → By Edibility Status
9 Format axes:
• Right-click X-axis → Edit Axis → Title = Stem Height (cm)
• Right-click Y-axis → Title = Stem Width (mm)
10 Tooltip:
Height: <stem-height> cm
Width: <stem-width> mm
Edibility: <Edibility Status>
Cap color: <cap-color>
Habitat: <habitat>
11 Add to dashboard with lasso selection enabled (default in Tableau Public)

🌡️ Chart 4 – Season × Habitat Heatmap (Edibility Rate)

Step Action
1 Create a new worksheet → name it 4_SeasonHabitat_Heatmap
2 Drag habitat to Columns
3 Drag season to Rows
4 Change Mark type to Square
5 Create edibility rate calculated field:
• Right-click in Data pane → Create Calculated Field → Name = Edibility Rate %
• Formula:
SUM(IF [Edibility Status] = 'Edible' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / ([Number of Records]) * 100
6 Drag Edibility Rate % to Color on the Marks card
7 Format color:
• Click Color → Edit Colors
• Palette: Green (or Red-Green Diverging)
• Check Stepped Color (optional, e.g., 4 steps)
8 Drag Edibility Rate % to Label → Format to 1 decimal + add % symbol
9 Tooltip:
• Season: <season>
• Habitat: <habitat>
• Edible: <CNT(IF [Edibility Status]='Edible' THEN 1 END)>
• Total: <CNT(Number of Records)>
• Edibility rate: <Edibility Rate %>%
10 Rename headers if needed (capitalize seasons: spring → Spring, etc.)

4 Step-by-Step Dashboard Assembly & Actions

4.1 Create Dashboard Layout and Populate with Individual Charts

Step Action
Create Dashboard
1 Click New Dashboard → name Mushroom Safety Explorer
2 Set dashboard size: Desktop → 1000 x 800 (or Automatic)
Add Sheets to Dashboard
3 Drag 1_Edibility_Donut → top-left
4 Drag 2_CapColor_StackedBar → top-right
5 Drag 3_Stem_Scatter → middle (full width)
6 Drag 4_SeasonHabitat_Heatmap → bottom (full width)

Note: At this point, we need to rearrange and resize and other tweaks to place individual interconnected charts to overall design


4.2 Add Dashboard Actions (Interactivity)

Action 1 – Edibility Filter (Chart Q1 → All others)

Step Action
1 Dashboard → Actions → Add Action → Filter
2 Name: Filter by Edibility
3 Source: 1_Edibility_Donut
4 Target: 2_CapColor_StackedBar, 3_Stem_Scatter, 4_SeasonHabitat_Heatmap
5 Run on: Select
6 Target Filters: All Fields → Edibility Status

Action 2 – Cap Color Filter (Chart Q2 → Charts Q3, Q4)

Step Action
1 Add new action → Filter
2 Name: Filter by Cap Color
3 Source: 2_CapColor_StackedBar
4 Target: 3_Stem_Scatter, 4_SeasonHabitat_Heatmap
5 Run on: Select
6 Target Filters: Selected Fields → cap-color

Action 3 – Scatter Brush Filter (Chart Q3 → Chart Q4)

Step Action
1 Add new action → Filter
2 Name: Brush to Heatmap
3 Source: 3_Stem_Scatter
4 Target: 4_SeasonHabitat_Heatmap
5 Run on: Select (lasso/box works automatically)
6 Target Filters: All Fields

Action 4 – Heatmap Reverse Filter (Chart Q4 → Chart Q3)

Step Action
1 Add new action → Filter
2 Name: Heatmap to Scatter
3 Source: 4_SeasonHabitat_Heatmap
4 Target: 3_Stem_Scatter
5 Run on: Select
6 Target Filters: All Fields

4.3 Add Clear Filters Button

Step Action
1 Dashboard → Add Object → Button (or Extension → Reset Filters)
2 If no native button: Add a text box with ✖ Clear All Filters → Dashboard → Actions → Add Filter action with all sheets as source AND target, then exclude from that action
3 Alternative: Use Show/Hide filters to manually clear

Remarks: A few final modifications to the dashboard are needed to prepare the version that will be embedded in the report, as outlined below.

Remarks: Two Important Remarks for Embedding a Published Dashboard into an R Markdown Document

  • Use a single-cell HTML table for embedding: It is recommended to create a single-cell HTML table and place the dashboard embedding code inside that cell. This approach makes it easier to control the alignment and positioning of the dashboard within the report.

  • Clean the copied embedding code before use: To avoid embedding errors, the code copied from the published dashboard should be cleaned and reformatted as shown below. This ensures that the dashboard is displayed correctly in the R Markdown document.


In summary, by integrating both numerical and categorical variables, the dashboard enables users to create a range of visualizations, including histograms, scatter plots, frequency tables, and pie charts. Through reactive filters, users can dynamically explore patterns such as how cap shape, gill attachment, habitat, or season correlate with toxicity.

5 Tableau Story Point

A Tableau story point guides users through key insights, such as highlighting which traits are most indicative of safety or danger. This interactive approach not only supports data-driven decision-making for foragers and mycologists but also demonstrates best practices in dashboard design, including clear labeling, tidy layout, and informative captions.

For illustrative purpose, we stay with the 4 individual charts to make a Tableau story point in the following steps.


New Story → Point 1 (Donut: Overview) → Point 2 (Bar: Color) → Point 3 (Scatter: Size) → Point 4 (Heatmap: Season) → Point 5 (Dashboard: Combined) → Present!


I will only provide the first point in the storyboard in detail. The rest of the points will be added similarly to the storyboard.


Create the Story Container

Action Instructions
Click New Story tab Bottom of Tableau workspace (icon: window with “+”)
Name your story Double-click “Story 1” → type Mushroom Safety Story
Set story size In lower-left corner, choose Desktop (1000 x 800) or custom size


Point 1 – The Big Picture

Element Your Content
Worksheet/Dashboard Donut
Caption/Headline Click “Add a caption” → Type: “Among 61,069 mushrooms, what proportion is safe to eat?”
Annotation/Text Drag “Drag to add text” from left pane → Place below chart → Type: “Only about 45% are edible – foraging requires careful identification.”
Interaction (e.g., “Hover over slices to see exact counts.”)
Filter Applied? None


After adding all individual charts to the storyboard, save your work and publish it to Tableau Public. You will need to sign in to your Tableau Public account to complete this step.

Once published, you can find the storyboard in your Tableau Public profile. Click the Share link to obtain the embed code, then paste the code into your RMarkdown file and clean it as needed. Finally, knit the RMarkdown file to HTML to generate the final output.
